+// RUN: triton-opt --split-input-file --add_multi_buffer_inner_scope %s | FileCheck %s

+// The pass appends an i32 iteration counter independently of the user while
+// induction variable. Check that its increment and yielded value stay i32,
+// while index, i32 and i64 user induction variables retain their own types.
+// Buffer polling may be inserted between the two independent increments.
+
+// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @inner_counter_index
+// CHECK: scf.while {{.*}} : (tensor<128xf32>, index, i32) -> (tensor<128xf32>, index, i32)
+// CHECK: ^bb0(%{{[^:]+}}: tensor<128xf32>, %[[IV_INDEX:[^:]+]]: index, %[[COUNT_INDEX:[^:]+]]: i32):
+// CHECK: %[[ONE_INDEX:[^ ]+]] = arith.constant {{.*}} 1 : i32
+// CHECK-NEXT: %[[NEXT_COUNT_INDEX:[^ ]+]] = arith.addi %[[COUNT_INDEX]], %[[ONE_INDEX]] {{.*}}ssbuffer.iterCounter{{.*}} : i32
+// CHECK: %[[NEXT_IV_INDEX:[^ ]+]] = arith.addi %[[IV_INDEX]], %{{[^ ]+}} : index
+// CHECK-NEXT: scf.yield %{{[^,]+}}, %[[NEXT_IV_INDEX]], %[[NEXT_COUNT_INDEX]] : tensor<128xf32>, index, i32
+
+module attributes {hacc.target = #hacc.target<"Ascend950PR_9579">, ssbuffer.intra_buf_count = 2 : i32} {
+  func.func @inner_counter_index() {
+    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
+    %c10 = arith.constant 10 : index
+    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
+    %cst_zero = arith.constant 0.0 : f32
+    %init = tensor.empty() : tensor<128xf32>
+    %carry = linalg.fill ins(%cst_zero : f32) outs(%init : tensor<128xf32>) -> tensor<128xf32>
+    scope.scope : () -> () {
+      %result:2 = scf.while (%arg0 = %carry, %arg1 = %c0)
+          : (tensor<128xf32>, index) -> (tensor<128xf32>, index) {
+        %cmp = arith.cmpi slt, %arg1, %c10 {ssbuffer.block_id = 16 : i32} : index
+        scf.condition(%cmp) %arg0, %arg1 : tensor<128xf32>, index
+      } do {
+      ^bb0(%arg0: tensor<128xf32>, %arg1: index):
+        %alloc = memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 7 : i32} : memref<128xf32>
+        %prod = bufferization.to_tensor %alloc {ssbuffer.block_id = 7 : i32} : memref<128xf32> to tensor<128xf32>
+        %consumed = arith.addf %prod, %prod {ssbuffer.block_id = 10 : i32} : tensor<128xf32>
+        %next = arith.addi %arg1, %c1 : index
+        scf.yield %consumed, %next : tensor<128xf32>, index
+      } attributes {ssbuffer.main_loop = 1 : i64, ssbuffer.block_id = 23 : i32}
+      scope.return
+    } {hivm.tcore_type = #hivm.tcore_type<VECTOR>}
+    return
+  }
+
+}

[triton-dist](feat) update triton distributed commit id (#3030)

(cherry picked from commit 1524bdf8a23a6a95a428abfe1cdf9a084d04ea60)

[ascend](feat) add AVE-backed TLA SIMD memory and widening ops (#2977)

* [ascend](feat) add AVE-backed TLA SIMD memory and widening ops

Expose pld/pst through AVE predicate loads/stores, 16/32-bit vgather
and vld through VFGatherOp, and strided integer vunpack through
VFExtSIOp/VFExtUIOp. Preserve predicate subview offsets and exact
32/16/8-byte stores. Keep output masking separate from widening's
source predicate and omit unnecessary selects for unmasked results.

Byte gathers, contiguous-half unpack, native predicate transforms,
register permutation, group reductions and scatter are outside this
change. No frontend LLVM intrinsic calls or pipeline changes are added.

Validation on base 836931296 plus this change: standalone wheel build;
169 frontend contracts; 534 new checks (339 numeric, 84 compile/run,
111 IR) on physical device 1 of the 63 host, Ascend950PR with CANN
9.2.0-beta.2; 12 adjacent vcvt/vpack/predicate checks. No simulator.
External bishengir-compile is 2.0.0, ff04a33ad9cd; the embedded dialect
submodule remains 4eb12142. The final documentation-only delta has an
identical runtime AST. No performance benchmark was performed.

* [Ascend](feat) add explicit TLA allocation spaces

Expose AddressSpace and the scope keyword while preserving legacy space calls. Mark independent allocations mem_unique and document Cube scope and native allocation limits. Reserve scale-factor spaces with an explicit unsupported diagnostic until HIVM defines their representation.

Validate allocation IR, compilation and device accuracy (9 passed), Cube GEMM and DMA regressions (112 passed, 2 existing padding skips), and memory planning overflow without fallback reuse.

[TritonToGraph](feat) implement RFC #2686 (scan + query-row lift) (#3024)

* [TritonToGraph](feat) add the SelectedBlockScan rule identity, facts and matcher

Selected-block scan is the #2686 rule that turns the table-indexed sparse gather
loop into a token-order scan.  This commit brings the identity and the matcher:

- rule bit 65536, its own SelectedBlockScan phase (after ConvertModuloToMask,
  before ProgramMapping), the factory declaration and the Python mirror.  The
  bit is fixed default-off as RFC #2686 requires, so the default mask stays 3071;
  SelectedBlockScanRule has no landing path of its own, which the rule body
  enforces by always going through the row lift.
- SelectedBlockScanFacts.h: the facts the matcher proves, the ScanCandidate that
  aggregates the builder-facing ones, and the four shared entry points.
  QueryRowBatching.h carries the joint entry the scan rewrite calls.
- the matcher: six parsers, one fact each, plus validateScan for every tie-out
  between them.  It compares values rather than syntax -- the per-iteration index
  load is cut out of both dependence walks, which is why the K/V tiles count as
  pid-independent, and loop-invariant scalar loads count as per-program
  constants, which makes the varlen dispatch reachable.  A miss is a silent
  nullopt with no diagnostics and no IR change.

* [TritonToGraph](feat) rewrite the gather loop and commit it through the joint gate

The rewriter emits one template per carried-state form: online softmax keeps
three iter args and the safe_m guard, additive dQ keeps one accumulator and
lands its contribution through the dot's C operand.  Both read the index table
once as a vector, clamp the padded lane to the last valid slot and turn the
selection into a per-token weight, so the scf.if guard becomes a zero weight.
BN = max(64, BS) for the forward form and BN = BS for the additive one, whose
transposed K is retained for a third dot.  The weight multiplies p in f32 before
the bf16 truncation and safe_m only ever subtracts, so the yielded m stays the
true maximum.

The driver keeps the rewrite in a private sandbox: clone, re-match, rebuild,
cleanup and verify, two on-chip budget gates (UB with the backend's multi-buffer
replication factor, and L0A/L0B/L0C) before and after the joint row lift, then a
commit-contract check that refuses a grid contract and an in-kernel flat program
id at the same time.  The sandbox is handed to the row lift's materialize entry
and dropped if it declines, so a decline leaves the live IR and its diagnostics
untouched and apply() cannot fail.  Build and registration follow.

* [TritonToGraph](test) add the NSA fixtures and pin the rewritten shape

Fixtures are real kernel TTIR (what graph-optimize sees in production) or a
one-knob mutation of one: forward dense / dynamic-NS / H==1 / varlen, the
padded-table S=17 case, the backward dQ form in both tile spellings, and the
static-grid capture.

nsa_selected_block_scan.mlir pins the target shape against the compiled gold
standard, the joint scan + row-lift form, and the rule-mask equality
65536 == 196608; the driver file pins the option whitelist, the unknown-bit
rejection and the static-grid contract; the budget file pins the UB/L0 warnings
and that a declined form stays byte-identical.

* [TritonToGraph](test) pin every matcher decline and the attribution guard

The negative file drives the refused shapes (two guards, extra loop load,
masked index load, flat table, ambiguous pid, forward transpose, non-zero
other, S > 4096, trip mismatch, non-power-of-two BS, grid-dependent rhs, causal
shift, tile wider than a block, folded offset, H > 1 head split, min combiner)
and requires byte-identical IR with empty stderr, so an over-match cannot pass.

The attribution file proves rule-mask=0 and rule-mask=3071 leave every fixture
byte-for-byte unchanged, so a diff in this slot is attributable to the scan
rewrite alone.  pytest covers the two mask whitelists, the fixed default-off
contract, the unknown-bit rejection and the 65536 == 196608 equality.

* [TritonToGraph](refactor) extract the row-lifting engine into a shared component

Move the generic part of DotRowCoalescing (row-dimension prepending,
per-row bound inference, loop rebuilding and the row-invariant clone
path) into RowLiftBuilder so other rules can reuse it.  DotRow keeps
only its matcher and the dot/store specific rewrite, and its output
stays unchanged.

* [graph-optimize](feat) finish the NSA row lift: Rule B, flat compute and wide-accumulator split

Bring the row lift in line with the reference implementation beyond the
extracted engine:

- add QueryRowBatchingRule (rule bit 131072) and register it under
  Rules/QueryRowBatchingRule.cpp, with the row-count policy bounded by
  L0A/L0C, UB peak and the physical core count (core_num now reaches the
  pass through compiler.py, triton_ascend.cc and ResourceSnapshot)
- lift tt.reduce and row-invariant scf.if, expand Q/O tensor pointers into
  pointer tensors, and read the selected-block index table once per row
- keep O/lse masked stores and the loop-carried state in the flat layout so
  no per-iteration reshape appears inside the loop
- split output accumulators wider than one vector register into two halves
- turn both #2686 rule bits on by default (default rule mask 199679)

+// The facts of SelectedBlockScanRule (#2686, rule bit 65536): what the scan
+// rewrite matches on, the candidate that aggregates the facts, and the four
+// entry points its three translation units share.
+//
+// Naming used across these files: "the scan rewrite" is this rule (rule bit
+// 65536, SelectedBlockScanRule); "the row lift" is QueryRowBatchingRule (rule
+// bit 131072), which the scan rewrite always materializes in its own sandbox.
+// RFC #2686 calls these two rules A and B; this tree says SelectedBlockScanRule
+// (the scan rewrite) and QueryRowBatchingRule (the row lift).
+//
+// No logic and no IR walking live here. The matcher, the rewriter and the
+// driver shell are separate translation units and each documents its own
+// sections; ScanCandidate is the only value that crosses from one to the next.
+//
+// The matcher is six parsers plus validateScan, one fact each, with no shared
+// mutable state:
+//
+//   parseLoop        (fn)                    -> LoopFact
+//   parseRowPosition (fn, loop)              -> RowFact          (matcher only)
+//   parseIndexTable  (fn, loop, row)         -> TableFact
+//   parseRecurrence  (loop, row)             -> recurrence fact  (variant)
+//   parseTiles       (loop, row, recurrence) -> tiles fact       (variant)
+//   parseCausalMask  (recurrence)            -> MaskFact         (matcher only)
+//   validateScan     (all facts)             -> every tie-out between them
+//
+// The order is data dependence, and the signatures say so: a parser takes the
+// facts it reads and returns the one it produces. Two knots keep both of their
+// sides inside one parser instead of being cross-checked later: the causal row
+// position and the table row (the same program id, so one fact), and the table
+// address with its row length (one address chain). The candidate is the
+// composition of the builder-facing facts; the matcher-only ones never leave
+// the matcher.
+
+#ifndef TRITON_TO_GRAPH_SELECTED_BLOCK_SCAN_FACTS_H
+#define TRITON_TO_GRAPH_SELECTED_BLOCK_SCAN_FACTS_H
+
+#include "TritonToGraph/GraphOptimizationRule.h"
+
+#include "mlir/Dialect/Arith/IR/Arith.h"
+#include "mlir/Dialect/SCF/IR/SCF.h"
+#include "mlir/IR/BuiltinOps.h"
+#include "mlir/Support/LogicalResult.h"
+#include "triton/Dialect/Triton/IR/Dialect.h"
+
+#include <algorithm>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <optional>
+#include <variant>
+
+namespace mlir {
+namespace triton {
+namespace cfg {
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// [Fact] The gather loop.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+struct LoopFact {
+  scf::ForOp forOp;     // the only scf.for, at the function body's top level
+  unsigned carried = 0; // loop-carried tensor values: 3 (fwd) or 1 (bwd)
+};
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// [Fact] The index table: where this program's row is, and how long it is.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+struct TableFact {
+  // The row-base pointer. Null when the front end folded the row advance into
+  // the in-loop address; the rewriter then re-creates the base from
+  // root + rowOffset before the vectorized read.
+  Value base;
+  Value root;         // the pointer the row base is offset from
+  Value rowOffset;    // loop-invariant row offset: program row + head slot
+  int64_t length = 0; // S, the row length in slots
+};
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// [Fact] The additive (bwd dq) tile address: everything the rewriter needs to
+// re-emit one masked `addptr` tile load at a different token start.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+struct AddPtrTile {
+  Value base;               // scalar pointer, loop-invariant and load-free
+  Value freeVec;            // [F] integer vector, loop-invariant
+  Value freeBoundRhs;       // [F,1] tensor the free-axis mask compares against
+  Value tokenBound;         // scalar bound of the "tokens < T" mask
+  Value blockStart;         // idx*BS: the value the causal mask also uses
+  unsigned tokenWidth = 32; // width of the token arithmetic: 32 or 64
+  int64_t tokenStride = 0;  // stride of one token along the address
+  int64_t freeExtent = 0;   // F, the tile's free-axis extent
+  int64_t blockSize = 0;    // BS, the tile's token extent
+};
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// [Fact] The carried-state recurrence. The variant IS the rewrite template:
+// nothing else records the choice, so the two can never disagree.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Online softmax (fwd): three iter args (o, m, l); m is updated with maxnumf
+// and the state is rescaled by exp(m_old - m_new).
+struct OnlineSoftmaxRecurrence {
+  triton::DotOp scoreDot; // dot(q, k, 0)
+  triton::DotOp valueDot; // dot(cast(p), v, o * alpha)
+  unsigned oArg = 0;      // carried-state roles, in iter-argument order
+  unsigned mArg = 0;
+  unsigned lArg = 0;
+  // The float width cast accepted around p, recorded as a direction rather
+  // than as the original op: the rewriter re-emits the same cast.
+  bool pCastIsExtend = false;
+};
+
+// Additive (bwd dq): one carried accumulator; the contribution lands in it
+// through the dot's C operand and the neutral element is 0. It is always iter
+// argument 0 (LoopFact::carried == 1 for this form), so no role index is
+// recorded.
+struct AdditiveRecurrence {
+  triton::DotOp scoreDot;      // dot(q, k, 0)
+  triton::DotOp valueDot;      // dot(dO, v, 0)
+  triton::DotOp accDot;        // dot(ds, k^T, acc)
+  triton::TransOp transpose;   // k^T, order replayed verbatim
+  Value lseVec;                // [G] f32, loop-invariant
+  Value deltaVec;              // [G] f32, loop-invariant
+  bool dsCastIsExtend = false; // ds was widened, not narrowed
+};
+
+// The variant is a deliberate deviation from the rest of Rules/, where a form
+// is an `enum class` field of one merged struct (IndependentAxisTensorizeRule's
+// TensorizeFormMatch is the clearest example). A tag and a merged struct leave
+// the other alternative's fields readable, and a rewriter that reads one still
+// compiles; a variant makes exactly one alternative exist at a time, so the
+// dispatch is exhaustive by construction and no field of the form not being
+// emitted can be touched.
+using RecurrenceFact =
+    std::variant<OnlineSoftmaxRecurrence, AdditiveRecurrence>;
+
+// ---- Accessors for the two dots both templates build on. ----
+
+inline triton::DotOp scoreDotOf(const RecurrenceFact &r) {
+  return std::visit([](const auto &f) { return f.scoreDot; }, r);
+}
+
+inline triton::DotOp valueDotOf(const RecurrenceFact &r) {
+  return std::visit([](const auto &f) { return f.valueDot; }, r);
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// [Fact] How the K/V tiles are addressed. The variant IS the spelling: the
+// rewriter has one emitter per spelling and dispatches on it.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// tt.make_tensor_ptr: the token axis is one of the view's offsets.
+struct MptrTiles {
+  triton::LoadOp kLoad;
+  triton::LoadOp vLoad;
+  triton::MakeTensorPtrOp kPtr;
+  triton::MakeTensorPtrOp vPtr;
+  unsigned kTokenAxis = 0;
+  unsigned vTokenAxis = 0;
+  int64_t blockSize = 0; // BS, the idx multiplier
+  // The only loop-carried address computation, re-created outside the loop.
+  // Filled for every make_tensor_ptr spelling, not only for the online-softmax

+  // spelled this way reads them too.
+  Value dynamicBoundResult; // null when the bound is already outside
+  Value dynamicBoundInput;  // null together with dynamicBoundResult
+};
+
+// Two nested tt.addptr's plus an explicit mask and other = 0.
+struct AddPtrTiles {
+  triton::LoadOp kLoad;
+  triton::LoadOp vLoad;
+  AddPtrTile kTile;
+  AddPtrTile vTile;
+  int64_t blockSize = 0; // BS, the idx multiplier
+};
+
+using TilesFact = std::variant<MptrTiles, AddPtrTiles>;
+
+// ---- Accessors over the two variants. The rewriter's two spelling emitters
+// ---- take their variant directly (each needs several fields, and dispatching
+// ---- once is clearer than dispatching per field); these are for the callers
+// ---- that need one field without caring which spelling produced it: the
+// ---- shared weight builder and the driver's identity check. ----
+
+inline triton::LoadOp kTileLoad(const TilesFact &tiles) {
+  return std::visit([](const auto &t) { return t.kLoad; }, tiles);
+}
+
+inline triton::LoadOp vTileLoad(const TilesFact &tiles) {
+  return std::visit([](const auto &t) { return t.vLoad; }, tiles);
+}
+
+inline int64_t tileBlockSize(const TilesFact &tiles) {
+  return std::visit([](const auto &t) { return t.blockSize; }, tiles);
+}
+
